title: Baseline Telemetry Anchoring and Eval Seed Management
author: Aisha K. Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood's baseline telemetry anchoring approach and a standardized eval seed management lifecycle. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs, and applied ML owners responsible for evaluation stability, promotion gating, and regression triage. The goal is to reduce spurious variance in continuous evals and make failure modes easier to diagnose by controlling seed sources, telemetry baselines, and anchoring strategies across private/dedicated/hosted targets.

Why this matters

- Small changes in RNG seeds, tokenization seeding, and probe sampling can inflate perceived variance and trigger false positive regressions.
- Anchored telemetry provides a persistent baseline that is resilient to benign nondeterminism while still surfacing meaningful quality regressions.
- Standardized seed management enables reproducible replays for triage and quantization regression investigations.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to production-facing eval harnesses, long-running shadow evals, and nightly synthesis jobs used for model promotion decisions.
- Does not replace deterministic unit tests or model-level determinism efforts — it complements them by controlling sampling and anchoring at the eval orchestration layer.
- Assumes eval platform can accept explicit RNG seeds and deterministic dataset shuffling parameters.

Key concepts and definitions

- Anchor set: a small, curated subset of probes used as a stable reference point (typical size: 500–2,000 probes depending on workload).
- Seed manifest: a versioned file that enumerates RNG seeds, shuffle salts, and the indices used to sample anchors and dynamic probes.
- Telemetry anchor vector: the vector of baseline metric values (e.g., BLEU, ROUGE, semantic-similarity, latency median) computed over the anchor set for a given model artifact and promotion point.
- Seed rotation window: controlled cadence for refreshing the seed manifest (default: quarterly for anchors, weekly for synthetic probes).

Guidelines and requirements

1) Anchor set creation and stewardship
   - Ownership: each product or workload team must nominate an anchor steward (primary + backup).
   - Composition: anchors must cover: 
     * 60% high-frequency, high-impact real traffic slices
     * 25% edge / long-tail / adversarial seeds identified from incidents
     * 15% synthetic stress probes (long context, function calls, multimodal where applicable)
   - Annotation: each anchor must have a metadata row (probe id | slice | origin | rationale | sensitivity flag). Use the anchor manifest template in the examples section below.

2) Seed manifest format and storage
   - Format: JSONL or CSV with columns: manifest_version, seed_id, rng_seed, shuffle_salt, probe_indices, created_by, created_at, role (anchor|dynamic|synthetic).
   - Storage: manifests are stored in the eval bucket under path: s3://redwood-evals/manifests/{team}/{workload}/{manifest_version}. Lock each manifest with an immutable tag once used for a promotion gate.

3) Telemetry anchoring calculation
   - Metric computation: compute telemetry anchor vector using the exact seed manifest and the same model runtime config (quant, kv-cache policy, batch config).
   - Aggregation: report median and 10/90 percentiles for latency; mean and std for quality metrics where meaningful.
   - Baseline window: maintain a rolling baseline history for the last 6 promotion points. Use EWMA with alpha=0.2 to smooth short-lived fluctuations.

4) Seed rotation and freshness policy
   - Anchor rotation: rotate anchor indices no more frequently than every 90 days unless a triggered incident requires emergency replacement. Document reason and vote in the rotation changelog.
   - Dynamic seed refresh: dynamic probe seed manifests may be refreshed weekly for sampling diversity; each refresh must have a different manifest_version and be recorded in telemetry.

5) Promotion and gating protocol
   - Promotion gate input: automated promotion jobs must reference an immutable manifest_version. The gate compares the new candidate telemetry anchor vector against the preserved baseline vector.
   - Acceptance criteria: candidate model must not show a statistically significant degradation on more than N slices in the anchor set (N defaults to 2 for 500-1k anchor size). Use bootstrap resampling (B=1,000) and require p > 0.05 for no-regression.
   - Quality-coverage check: if a candidate improves aggregate metrics but worsens a high-sensitivity anchor (sensitivity flag set), require a product sign-off.

6) Reproducible replay for triage
   - Repro command: provide the exact CLI and environment file to replay an anchor run. Example: 
     
     eval-run --manifest s3://redwood-evals/manifests/vision-team/recommendation/v3-manifest-2026-01-12.jsonl \n       --model-ref model-registry://prod/recommendation/v2.3.1 \n       --runtime-config runtimes/quantized-gpu.yaml \n       --replay-output /tmp/replays/replay-20260210-001.jsonl

   - Determinism checklist:
     1. Use the exact manifest_version.
     2. Use pinned model artifact digest (not tag).
     3. Use the same runtime image and kernel revision.
     4. Record and compare seed hash between original and replayed runs.

Operational playbooks

- Daily smoke: the eval platform posts a daily anchor vector summary to #eval-telemetry. On-call evaluator checks for any drift >2x EWMA sigma on critical anchors.

- Regression triage fast path:
  1. Triage engineer compares candidate anchor vector to baseline and runs reproducible replay using the manifest_version.
  2. If replay reproduces regression, attach replay artifacts to a regression issue and assign to model owner.
  3. If replay does not reproduce, escalate to platform SRE to check runtime/kernel/version mismatch, quant artifact mismatch, or nondeterministic RNG sources.

- Emergency anchor replacement: when anchor probes are found compromised (PII leak, invalidated by product change), the steward can replace up to 10% of anchors outside regular rotation. Log a post-hoc review within 48 hours.

Metrics, SLOs and alerts

- Anchor stability SLO: 99% of daily anchor vector differences must be within the EWMA 3-sigma band across a 30-day window.
- Alerting: create PagerDuty alert when:
  * a single critical anchor drops by >5% absolute in quality or increases latency by >50% p95, or
  * more than 3 anchors cross the statistical regression threshold during a promotion attempt.

Examples and templates

- Anchor manifest snippet (JSONL row):
  {"manifest_version": "anchor-v1-2026-01", "seed_id": "anchor-0001", "rng_seed": "9823749283", "shuffle_salt": "slt-04", "probe_indices": "[13,56,234,1021]", "created_by": "aisha.patel@redwood.ai", "created_at": "2026-01-10", "role": "anchor"}

- Example telemetry anchor table (text table):
  | probe_slice | metric | baseline_value | candidate_value | delta | sensitivity | action |
  | high-frequency-search | semantic-sim | 0.842 | 0.835 | -0.007 | high | product-review |
  | long-context-chain | pass-rate | 0.912 | 0.885 | -0.027 | critical | block-promotion |

- Runtime config YAML excerpt (used for replay):
  image: gcr.io/redwood-eval-images/eval-runtime:2026-01-28
  kernel_rev: k1.7.3
  quant_profile: 8bit-lora-v2
  kv_cache_policy: preserve-full

Roles and responsibilities

- Anchor steward (team): maintains anchor set, manages seed manifest lifecycle, documents rotation rationale.
- Model owner: validates candidate regressions and approves or rejects promotion after triage.
- Eval platform SRE: ensures manifest immutability, provides replay tooling, and diagnoses nondeterministic platform causes.
- Applied ML ops: monitors anchor SLOs and coordinates cross-team investigations.

Change log and governance

- All manifest changes require an entry in the manifest-changelog.md and a 2-person review (steward + product or senior ML engineer).
- Governance board: triage council meets monthly to review anchor slippage trends and approve exceptional rotations.

Appendix: small reproducibility checklist

- Confirm manifest_version and seed hash
- Confirm model digest (sha256) and runtime image digest
- Confirm quant/precision flags used in the original run
- Re-run replay with debug telemetry enabled (token-level hashes, deterministic RNG) for 3 runs and compare inter-run variance
